claim: Single-cell expression profiling reveals extensive cell-to-cell variability at the transcriptomic and proteomic level.
source: Extensive cell-to-cell variability at the transcriptomic and proteomic level has been one of the stand-out observations.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from single-cell expression profiling studies.

claim: Most experimental analyses of single cells are destructive, providing only snapshot data of cellular states.
source: Because most experimental analyses are destructive we only have access to snapshot data of cellular states.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of experimental methods.

claim: Loss of temporal information from destructive measurements presents significant challenges for inferring dynamics and causes of cell-to-cell variability.
source: This loss of temporal information presents significant challenges for inferring dynamics, as well as causes of cell-to-cell variability.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of destructive measurements.

claim: Dynamic variability from within cells (intrinsic noise) typically cannot be separated from variability across the population (extrinsic noise) using standard measurements.
source: In particular, we typically cannot separate dynamic variability from within cells ('intrinsic noise') from variability across the population ('extrinsic noise').
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of typical experimental approaches.

claim: Multiple generic reporters from the same biochemical pathways can infer magnitudes of intrinsic and extrinsic transcriptional noise.
source: We show that multiple generic reporters from the same biochemical pathways (e.g. mRNA and protein) can infer magnitudes of intrinsic and extrinsic transcriptional noise, identifying sources of heterogeneity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by mathematical derivations and simulations.

claim: Pathway-reporters compare favourably to the dual-reporter method.
source: Stochastic simulations support our theory, and demonstrate that 'pathway-reporters' compare favourably to the well-known, but often difficult to implement, dual-reporter method.
evidence: This is supported by stochastic simulation results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Noise is a fundamental aspect of every cellular process.
source: Noise is a fundamental aspect of every cellular process Shahrezaei and Swain, 2008b.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Noise can drive cell-fate transitions.
source: Frequently it is even of functional importance, for example in driving cell-fate transitions.
evidence: This is stated as a known functional role of noise.

claim: Noise can afford evolutionary advantages in the context of bet-hedging strategies.
source: Sometimes it can afford evolutionary advantages, for example, in the context of bet-hedging strategies.
evidence: This is stated as a known evolutionary role of noise.

claim: Gene expression noise is separable into intrinsic and extrinsic sources of variability.
source: Generally speaking, gene expression noise is separable into two sources of variability, as pioneered by Swain et al., 2002.
evidence: This is stated as an established framework with citation support.

claim: Intrinsic noise is generated by the dynamics of the gene expression process itself.
source: Intrinsic noise is generated by the dynamics of the gene expression process itself.
evidence: This is a definition of intrinsic noise.

claim: Extrinsic noise reflects variation in gene expression and transcription activity across the cell population.
source: Such sources of variability contribute extrinsic noise, and reflect the variation in gene expression and transcription activity across the cell population.
evidence: This is a definition of extrinsic noise.

claim: Long noncoding RNA can act as a transcriptional regulator.
source: the influence of long noncoding RNA as a transcriptional regulator Goodrich and Kugel, 2006
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Understanding extrinsic noise is central to understanding cell-population heterogeneity.
source: As such, understanding extrinsic noise lies at the heart of understanding cell-population heterogeneity.
evidence: This is stated as a logical consequence of the definition of extrinsic noise.

claim: Identifying sources of gene expression noise from transcriptomic measurements alone has proven difficult.
source: So far, identifying the sources of gene expression noise from transcriptomic measurements alone has proven difficult Paulsson, 2004; Pedraza and Paulsson, 2008.
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge with citation support.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing is destructive.
source: The fundamental hindrance lies in the fact that single-cell RNA sequencing, which provides most of the available data, is destructive, so that datasets reflect samples from across a population, rather than samples taken repeatedly from the same cell.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the experimental method.

claim: Temporal information is lost in single-cell RNA sequencing measurements.
source: As temporal information is lost in such measurements Komorowski et al., 2011, it may be impossible to distinguish temporal variability within individual cells (e.g. burstiness), from ensemble variability across the population (i.e. extrinsic noise).
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of destructive measurements with citation support.

claim: Systems with intrinsic noise alone can exhibit behaviour indistinguishable from systems with both extrinsic and intrinsic noise.
source: A number of numerical and experimental studies have suggested this confounding effect Jones and Elf, 2018; Jones et al., 2014; Zopf et al., 2013, showing that systems with intrinsic noise alone exhibit behaviour that is indistinguishable from systems with both extrinsic and intrinsic noise.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies with citation support.

claim: The moment scaling behaviour and transcript distribution may be indistinguishable from situations with purely intrinsic noise.
source: This is examined more formally in Ham et al., 2020a, where we show that the moment scaling behaviour and transcript distribution may be indistinguishable from situations with purely intrinsic noise.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors with citation support.

claim: It is impossible to identify the sources of variability from observed transcript abundance distributions alone.
source: We are able to prove rigorously that it is in general impossible to identify the sources of variability, and consequently, the underlying transcription dynamics, from observed transcript abundance distributions alone.
evidence: This is stated as a primary theoretical result of the study.

claim: Systems with intrinsic noise alone can always present identically to similar systems with extrinsic noise.
source: Systems with intrinsic noise alone can always present identically to similar systems with extrinsic noise.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical result of the study.

claim: The non-identifiability effect does not depend on the precise choice of distribution.
source: For practical purposes, the effect does not appear to depend on the precise choice of distribution, but holds more generally.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study's analysis.

claim: Extrinsic noise invariably distorts the apparent degree of burstiness of the underlying system.
source: Moreover, we demonstrate that extrinsic noise invariably distorts the apparent degree of burstiness of the underlying system: data which seems 'bursty' is not necessarily generated by a bursty process, if there is cell-to-cell variability across the population.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study's analysis.

claim: Additional information beyond the observed copy number distribution is required to constrain the space of possible dynamics.
source: Our results highlight (in fact prove mathematically) the requirement for additional information, beyond the observed copy number distribution, in order to constrain the space of possible dynamics that could give rise to the same distribution.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the non-identifiability results.

claim: The dual-reporter method can separate noise into extrinsic and intrinsic components by observing correlations between expression of two independent, identically distributed fluorescent reporter genes.
source: In this approach, noise can be separated into extrinsic and intrinsic components, by observing correlations between the expression of two independent, but identically distributed fluorescent reporter genes.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the dual-reporter method from Swain et al., 2002.

claim: Dual-reporter assays have been employed experimentally to study noise contributed by both global and gene-specific effects.
source: Dual-reporter assays have been employed experimentally to study the noise contributed by both global and gene-specific effects Elowitz et al., 2002; Raser and O'Shea, 2005; Raj et al., 2006.
evidence: This is stated as a known application with citation support.

claim: Dual reporters are rarely identically regulated.
source: A particular challenge, however, is that dual reporters are rarely identically regulated Raj et al., 2006; Quarton et al., 2020, and are not straightforward to set up in every system.
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge with citation support.

claim: The independence of dual reporters cannot be guaranteed in some systems.
source: More recently, it has been shown that the independence of dual reporters cannot be guaranteed in some systems Naik et al., 2021.
evidence: This is stated as a recent finding with citation support.

claim: Non-identical and not-necessarily independent reporters can provide an analogous noise decomposition to dual reporters.
source: We demonstrate that non-identical and not-necessarily independent reporters can provide an analogous noise decomposition.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Measurements from the same biochemical pathway (e.g. mRNA and protein) can replace dual reporters for noise decomposition.
source: Our result shows that measurements taken from the same biochemical pathway (e.g. mRNA and protein) can replace dual reporters, enabling the noise decomposition to be obtained from a single gene.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding of the study.

claim: The pathway-reporter method circumvents the requirement of conditionally independent and identically regulated reporter genes.
source: This completely circumvents the requirement of conditionally independent and identically regulated reporter genes.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the pathway-reporter method.

claim: For constitutive expression, the results from the pathway-reporter decomposition are identical to those from dual reporters.
source: In the case of constitutive expression, the results obtained from our decomposition are identical to those obtained from dual reporters.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study's analysis.

claim: For bursty systems, the pathway-reporter approach provides a satisfactorily close approximation except in extreme cases.
source: For bursty systems, we show that our approach provides a satisfactorily close approximation, except in extreme cases.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study's analysis.

claim: The Telegraph model is a two-state model describing promoter switching, transcription, and mRNA degradation.
source: A simple model for stochastic mRNA dynamics is the Telegraph model: a two-state model describing promoter switching, transcription, and mRNA degradation.
evidence: This is a description of the Telegraph model.

claim: The Telegraph model was first introduced in Ko, 1991.
source: The Telegraph model was first introduced in Ko, 1991, and has since then been widely employed in the literature to model bursty gene expression in eukaryotic cells Bahar Halpern et al., 2015; So et al., 2011; Suter et al., 2011; Larsson et al., 2019.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The Telegraph model has been widely employed to model bursty gene expression in eukaryotic cells.
source: The Telegraph model was first introduced in Ko, 1991, and has since then been widely employed in the literature to model bursty gene expression in eukaryotic cells Bahar Halpern et al., 2015; So et al., 2011; Suter et al., 2011; Larsson et al., 2019.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: In the Telegraph model, the gene switches probabilistically between an active state and an inactive state at rates λ and μ, respectively.
source: In this model, the gene switches probabilistically between an active state and an inactive state, at rates λ (on-rate) and μ (off-rate), respectively.
evidence: This is a description of the Telegraph model dynamics.

claim: The steady-state distribution for the mRNA copy number in the Telegraph model can be explicitly calculated.
source: The steady-state distribution for the mRNA copy number can be explicitly calculated as Peccoud and Ycart, 1995
evidence: This is stated with citation support and followed by the mathematical formula.

claim: Constitutive gene expression is a limiting case of the Telegraph model when the off-rate μ is 0.
source: Constitutive gene expression is a limiting case of the Telegraph model, which arises when the off-rate μ is 0, so that the gene remains permanently in the active state.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the Telegraph model.

claim: Instantaneously bursty gene expression occurs when mRNA are produced in very short bursts with potentially prolonged periods of inactivity in between.
source: At the opposite extreme is instantaneously bursty gene expression in which mRNA are produced in very short bursts with potentially prolonged periods of inactivity in between.
evidence: This is a definition of instantaneously bursty gene expression.

claim: Instantaneously bursty gene expression has been frequently reported experimentally, particularly in mammalian genes.
source: This mode of gene expression has been frequently reported experimentally, particularly in mammalian genes Raj et al., 2006; Bahar Halpern et al., 2015; Suter et al., 2011; Larsson et al., 2019.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Transcriptional bursting can be treated as a limit of the Telegraph model where the off-rate μ tends to infinity while the on-rate λ remains fixed.
source: Transcriptional bursting may be treated as a limit of the Telegraph model, where the off-rate, μ, tends to infinity, while the on-rate λ remains fixed.
evidence: This is stated as a mathematical property of the Telegraph model.

claim: The compound distribution accounts for random cell-to-cell variation across a population.
source: We can account for random cell-to-cell variation across a population by way of a compound distribution Ham et al., 2020b
evidence: This is stated as a modeling approach with citation support.

claim: The compound model is a valid approximation for individual cells with dynamic parameters, provided these change sufficiently slower than the transcriptional dynamics.
source: This model is also a valid approximation for individual cells with dynamic parameters, provided these change sufficiently slower than the transcriptional dynamics Lenive et al., 2016.
evidence: This is stated as a condition for validity with citation support.

claim: Some primary sources of extrinsic noise have an autocorrelation time comparable to the cell cycle.
source: In the context of gene expression, it has been shown experimentally that some of the primary sources of extrinsic noise have an autocorrelation time comparable to the cell cycle Rosenfeld et al., 2005.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Differences in cell-cycle phases across the population are a significant source of heterogeneity.
source: A further significant source of heterogeneity arises from the differences in cell-cycle phases across the population Skinner et al., 2016.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Cell-cycle effects have been shown to obscure the precise underlying transcriptional dynamics.
source: Such effects have been shown to obscure the precise underlying transcriptional dynamics Zopf et al., 2013; Huh and Paulsson, 2011, and impede the inference of transcriptional parameters from experimental data Beentjes et al., 2020.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Any Telegraph distribution with fixed parameters can be identically obtained from a Telegraph distribution with parameter variation.
source: We first observe that any Telegraph distribution with fixed parameters can be identically obtained from a Telegraph distribution with parameter variation.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical result derived in the supplementary material.

claim: Any Telegraph distribution can be obtained by varying the transcription rate parameter on a narrower Telegraph distribution according to a scaled beta distribution.
source: Thus, any Telegraph distribution can be obtained by varying the transcription rate parameter on a narrower Telegraph distribution (i.e. with a smaller off-rate) according to a scaled beta distribution.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical result following from equation (3).

claim: The copy number distribution of an instantaneously bursty system can be obtained from both bursty and instantaneously bursty dynamics with appropriate parameter variation.
source: The previous result extends to instantaneously bursty systems. The copy number distribution of an instantaneously bursty system can be obtained from both bursty and instantaneously bursty dynamics, provided that there is appropriate parameter variation.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical result derived in the supplementary material.

claim: A compound Poisson distribution uniquely determines the compounding distribution.
source: It has long been known Feller, 1943 that a compound Poisson distribution uniquely determines the compounding distribution.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Noise on the transcription rate will invariably produce copy number data that is suggestive of a more bursty model.
source: The representations given in (3 – 5), however, show that both estimating parameters and the underlying dynamics from the form of the copy number distribution alone can be misleading. Noise on the transcription rate will invariably produce copy number data that is suggestive of a more bursty model.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the non-identifiability results.

claim: For practical purposes, any similar distribution to the specific noise distributions in the non-identifiability results will produce a similar effect.
source: It is of practical importance to recognise that, while the non-identifiability results (summarised in Table 1) are dependent on specific noise distributions, for practical purposes any similar distribution will produce a similar effect.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from simulations with truncated normal distributions.

claim: The effect of varying the transcription rate or burst intensity parameter according to a unimodal noise distribution is to produce copy number distributions that are generally consistent with systems that appear burstier.
source: In every case, the effect of varying the transcription rate or burst intensity parameter according to a unimodal noise distribution is to produce copy number distributions that are generally consistent with systems that appear burstier.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from simulations shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Static measurements of mRNA are not always sufficient to infer the underlying dynamics of gene activity.
source: Finally, we note that our results explain previous empirical observations that static measurements of mRNA are not always sufficient to infer the underlying dynamics of gene activity.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation provided by the study's results.

claim: The noise decomposition applies to dynamic noise.
source: The decomposition applies to dynamic noise Hilfinger and Paulsson, 2011, and generalises to higher moments in Hilfinger et al., 2012.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The noise decomposition is equivalent to the normalised Law of Total Variance.
source: As shown in Hilfinger and Paulsson, 2011, the noise decomposition is equivalent to the normalised Law of Total Variance (Ross, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Under certain conditions, the decomposition of total noise can be obtained from non-identically distributed and not-necessarily independent reporters.
source: We show that, under certain conditions, the decomposition in (6) can alternatively be obtained from non-identically distributed and not-necessarily independent reporters.
evidence: This is stated as a primary theoretical result of the study.

claim: The covariance of any two variables can be decomposed into the expectation of a conditional covariance and the covariance of two conditional expectations.
source: Our result relies on the observation that the covariance of any two variables can be decomposed into the expectation of a conditional covariance and the covariance of two conditional expectations (the Law of Total Covariance Ross, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support as a mathematical property.

claim: Stochastic simulations show excellent agreement between the pathway-reporter method and the dual-reporter method for constitutive expression.
source: Overall, we observe an excellent agreement between the results obtained by the pathway-reporter method, the dual-reporter method and the theoretical noise.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from simulations presented in Table 2.

claim: There is consistently slightly more variation in the pathway-reporter results compared with the dual-reporter results for constitutive expression.
source: There is consistently slightly more variation in the pathway-reporter results compared with the dual-reporter results.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from simulations presented in Table 2.

claim: The pathway-reporter method performs favourably compared to the dual-reporter method calculated from mature mRNA across a range of parameter combinations.
source: The pathway-reporter method performs favourably compared to the dual-reporter method calculated from mature mRNA, and consistently outperforms the dual-reporter method on nascent mRNA.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from simulations across 60 different parameter combinations.

claim: Despite mRNA and protein numbers not being strictly independent, they can replace dual reporters to decompose noise at the transcriptional level for practical purposes.
source: Thus, despite mRNA and protein numbers not being strictly independent, they can, for practical purposes, replace dual reporters to decompose the noise at the transcriptional level.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analysis and simulations.

claim: Both the pathway-reporter and dual-reporter methods show slower convergence when copy numbers are low.
source: We note that both the pathway-reporter (nascent-mature or mature-protein) and dual-reporter methods show slower convergence when copy numbers are low.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the simulations.

claim: Pathway reporters usually show fractionally slower convergence and fractionally more variation than a dual reporter.
source: Pathway reporters usually show fractionally slower convergence and fractionally more variation than a dual reporter, as suggested by the standard deviations in Tables 2 and 3.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the simulations.

claim: The most common mode of gene expression reported experimentally is burstiness.
source: The most common mode of gene expression that is reported experimentally is burstiness Jones and Elf, 2018; Raj et al., 2006; Bahar Halpern et al., 2015; Suter et al., 2011; Larsson et al., 2019; Golding et al., 2005, in which mRNA are produced in short bursts with periods of inactivity in between.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: In E. coli and yeast, mRNA are typically degraded within a few minutes, while most proteins have lifetimes at the level of 10s of minutes to hours.
source: In E. coli Taniguchi et al., 2010 and yeast Belle et al., 2006, for example, mRNA are typically degraded within a few minutes, while most proteins have lifetimes at the level of 10 s of minutes to hours.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Over 90% of genes with mean mRNA levels greater than 5 have a value for λ of at least 0.5 in mouse and human fibroblasts.
source: Of those genes with mean mRNA levels greater than 5, we found that over 90% have a value for λ of at least 0.5, and over 65% have a value for λ greater than 1.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from analysis of data from Larsson et al., 2019.

claim: Nascent-protein reporters will provide a satisfactory estimate of the extrinsic noise level for a substantial fraction of genes.
source: Thus, the heatmaps given in Figure 5 (top panel) suggest that nascent-protein reporters will provide a satisfactory estimate of the extrinsic noise level for a substantial fraction of genes.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the heatmap analysis and parameter estimates from the literature.

claim: The mature mRNA–protein reporters are less reliable than nascent-protein reporters, with the requirement of slow protein decay and higher on-rate being more pronounced.
source: The mature nRNA–protein reporters are less reliable, with the requirement of slow protein decay and higher on-rate being more pronounced than for the nascent mRNA–protein reporters; this is evident from Figure 5 (second panel).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the heatmap analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The results for nascent mRNA–protein reporters show comparable performance to dual reporters for bursty systems.
source: The results for the nascent mRNA–protein reporters, case (c), given in Table 4 show comparable performance to dual reporters, with only modest overshoot
evidence: This is stated as a finding from simulations presented in Table 4.

claim: The error heatmaps provide an accurate estimate of the overshoot in the nascent-protein results.
source: The error heatmaps of Figure 5 provide an accurate estimate of the overshoot in the nascent-protein results in Table 4.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from comparing heatmaps to simulation results.

claim: The pathway reporter approach is remarkably insensitive to the specific dynamics of mRNA and protein synthesis.
source: In summary, the results show that our pathway reporter approach is remarkably insensitive to the specific dynamics of mRNA and protein synthesis.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from validation on various gene expression models.

claim: The correlations between reporter pairs do not strongly depend on the details of the gene expression model used.
source: In particular, the correlations between reporter pairs do not strongly depend on the details of the gene expression model used.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from validation on various gene expression models.

claim: Multiple factors that contribute to mRNA heterogeneity can confound the measured distribution, which hinders analysis.
source: In particular, the multiple factors that contribute to mRNA heterogeneity can confound the measured distribution, which hinders analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge in the field.

claim: Population heterogeneity inflates the apparent burstiness of the system.
source: A particular feature of our non-identifiability results is that population heterogeneity inflates the apparent burstiness of the system.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the non-identifiability results.

claim: Additional work may be required to determine the true level of burstiness of the underlying system.
source: In particular, additional work may be required to determine the true level of burstiness of the underlying system.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the non-identifiability results.

claim: The Noise Decomposition Principle directly generalises the theoretical underpinnings of the dual reporter method.
source: Our Noise Decomposition Principle directly generalises the theoretical underpinnings of the dual reporter method and related approaches Bowsher and Swain, 2012; Jetka et al., 2018
evidence: This is stated as a contribution of the study.

claim: The pathway-reporter method is experimentally more easily implementable than the dual reporter method.
source: here we have used it to identify a practical approach—the pathway-reporter method—for obtaining an effective and experimentally more easily implementable noise decomposition.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the pathway-reporter method.

claim: The accuracy of the pathway-reporter method is provably identical to dual reporters for constitutive gene expression.
source: The accuracy of the pathway-reporter method is provably identical for constitutive gene expression
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical result of the study.

claim: For nascent-mature mRNA reporters, measurements are readily obtainable from current single-cell data.
source: and in the case of nascent-mature mRNA reporters, the measurements are readily obtainable from current single-cell data Shah et al., 2018; La Manno et al., 2018; Skinner et al., 2016.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: For bursty systems, the pathway-reporter method in general provides only an approximation of the extrinsic noise.
source: For bursty systems, the method in general provides only an approximation of the extrinsic noise.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method for bursty systems.

claim: One of the proposed pathway reporters provides a satisfactory estimate of the extrinsic noise for most genes.
source: We are, however, able to demonstrate computationally, that one of the proposed pathway reporters provides a satisfactory estimate of the extrinsic noise for most genes.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computational analysis.

claim: The pathway reporter method is independent of the specific dynamics of mRNA and protein synthesis.
source: Our results show that the pathway reporter method is independent of the specific dynamics of mRNA and protein synthesis, and therefore should be applicable to a broad range of experimental scenarios.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from validation on various models.

claim: The pathway-reporter approach relies on the assumption that extrinsic noise sources act independently.
source: In particular, the approach relies on the assumption that extrinsic noise sources act independently.
evidence: This is stated as an assumption of the method.

claim: The transcription and translation rates in E. coli may anticorrelate.
source: For example, it has been suggested Hilfinger et al., 2016; Cole and Luthey-Schulten, 2017 that the transcription and translation rates in E. coli anticorrelate.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Recent developments in single-cell profiling allow simultaneous measurements of transcripts and proteins in thousands of single cells.
source: Recent developments in single-cell profiling now allow simultaneous measurements of transcripts and proteins in thousands of single cells Stoeckius et al., 2017; Peterson et al., 2017; Reimegård et al., 2019.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Extrinsic noise distorts the multivariate copy number distribution of different species in the gene expression pathway.
source: Our work reveals that extrinsic noise distorts the multivariate copy number distribution of the different species in the gene expression pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Reliable estimates of noise strength will assist in setting better practices for model fitting and inference in the analysis of single-cell data.
source: We have exploited this to yield reliable estimates of noise strength, which we are confident will assist in setting better practices for model fitting and inference in the analysis of single-cell data.
evidence: This is stated as an expected impact of the study.

claim: A more nuanced analysis of the multivariate distribution may offer further insight into model and noise identifiability.
source: A more nuanced analysis of this multivariate distribution may offer even further insight into model and noise identifiability.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about future work.

claim: Extrinsic noise produces a visibly more correlated joint distribution of nascent-mature, nascent-protein, and mature-protein levels.
source: Extrinsic noise produces a visibly more correlated joint distribution, which forms the basis of the pathway-reporter method.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from Figure 3.

claim: Parameter values that reduce the delay between nascent mRNA, mature mRNA, and protein time series will tend to increase correlation.
source: Parameter values that reduce this delay will tend to increase correlation, and thereby increase the normalised intrinsic contribution to the covariance.
evidence: This is stated as an intuition about when correlation increases.

claim: When the system undergoes long timescale changes, copy numbers tend to drop to very low values for extended periods, contributing to high correlation between mRNA and protein.
source: A further contributor to high correlation between mRNA and protein, is when the system undergoes long timescale changes. In this situation, the copy numbers tend to drop to very low values for extended periods.
evidence: This is stated as an intuition about when correlation increases.

claim: The primary parameter influencing long timescale changes is the active-rate λ, specifically when λ tends to 0.
source: The primary parameter influencing this type of behaviour is the active-rate λ, specifically, when λ tends to 0 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C.
